question: Nursing is best described as a combination of which two disciplines?

options.A: A policy and a law
options.B: An art and a science
options.C: An experiment and a theory
options.D: A business and a trade

explanation: Nursing requires scientific knowledge combined with the artistic, human touch of compassionate care. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of professional nursing practice?

options.A: Optimizing health and preventing illness
options.B: Managing hospital finances and budgets
options.C: Prescribing major pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Diagnosing rare surgical diseases

explanation: Nurses focus heavily on promoting health, preventing illness, and caring for people across their lifespan. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h1)

question: Who famously described nursing as putting the patient in the best condition for nature to act?

options.A: Virginia Henderson
options.B: Dame Kofo Ademola
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Nnamdi Azikiwe

explanation: Florence Nightingale laid the foundation for modern nursing with her environmental theory and famous definitions of care. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h2)

question: According to modern definitions by bodies like the International Council of Nurses, who receives nursing care?

options.A: Individuals admitted only for infectious diseases
options.B: Both sick and well people in all settings
options.C: Only critically ill patients in tertiary hospitals
options.D: Patients recovering exclusively from major surgeries

explanation: Nursing goes beyond treating disease to include health promotion and wellness for healthy individuals across various environments. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which regulatory body authorizes and licenses nurses to practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body regulating the training and practice of nursing and midwifery in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h3)

question: A person has finished classroom lectures in a school of nursing, but has not yet passed the board exams or received a license. Can they practice independently as a nurse?

options.A: No, legal authorization by the regulatory council is required first
options.B: Yes, as long as they finished their classroom hours
options.C: Yes, under the direct verbal permission of a hospital owner
options.D: No, but they can independently prescribe simple medications

explanation: A nurse must be formally licensed and authorized by the national regulatory authority before practicing independently. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h3)

question: When a nurse explains to a pregnant mother the importance of sleeping under an insecticide-treated net, which role is the nurse performing?

options.A: Educator
options.B: Financial auditor
options.C: Surgical assistant
options.D: Hospital manager

explanation: Teaching patients how to prevent illness and manage their health falls directly under the educator role. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h4)

question: What does a nurse primarily do when acting as a patient advocate?

options.A: Pays the hospital bills on behalf of indigent patients
options.B: Makes legal binding contracts for the hospital management
options.C: Protects patient rights and safety within the healthcare system
options.D: Performs diagnostic laboratory tests without doctor orders

explanation: An advocate speaks up for the patient's best interests, ensuring they are safe and their rights are respected. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h4)

question: Who primarily introduced Western-style formal nursing training to Nigeria during the colonial era?

options.A: International trade merchants and explorers
options.B: Christian missionaries and colonial administrators
options.C: United Nations peacekeeping forces
options.D: Local traditional birth attendants and herbalists

explanation: Missionaries and the colonial government established the earliest Western hospitals and nursing schools in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of modern nursing in Nigeria today?

options.A: Regulation of practice standards by a statutory national council
options.B: Complete reliance on traditional herbalists for hospital policies
options.C: University degree programs offering Bachelor of Nursing Science
options.D: Specialized post-basic certifications in areas like midwifery and ICU

explanation: Modern professional nursing in Nigeria is an evidence-based, scientifically regulated discipline, not reliant on traditional herbalists. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h5)

question: Who primarily provided organized care for the sick during the early religious era of nursing?

options.A: Trained hospital administrators
options.B: Religious orders and monasteries
options.C: University-certified physicians
options.D: Government medical boards

explanation: Early organized healthcare facilities were predominantly established and managed by religious institutions and monastic groups before formal secular nursing schools emerged. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h1)

question: What best describes how healthcare was handled in traditional Nigerian societies before western medicine arrived?

options.A: Strictly regulated care inside government clinics
options.B: Paid services provided by foreign missionaries
options.C: Communal family care combined with herbal remedies
options.D: Isolated treatment managed only by trained surgeons

explanation: Traditional healing relied heavily on community support, family roles, and local herbs administered by elders or traditional healers. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which war helped Florence Nightingale prove the lifesaving impact of hospital sanitation?

options.A: World War I
options.B: The Nigerian Civil War
options.C: The American Civil War
options.D: The Crimean War

explanation: Nightingale gained international recognition and proved her theories on hygiene while managing military hospitals during the Crimean War. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h2)

question: What was the main focus of Florence Nightingale's environmental theory of nursing?

options.A: Focusing solely on the psychological state of the patient
options.B: Manipulating the patient's surroundings to enhance healing
options.C: Performing minor surgical procedures in the ward
options.D: Administering complex chemical drugs to cure infections

explanation: Her theory emphasized clean air, water, light, and quiet as the primary tools to put the patient in the best condition for nature to act. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h2)

question: Who introduced the earliest Western-style nursing and hospital care to Nigeria?

options.A: Christian missionary societies
options.B: Military combat units
options.C: The World Health Organization
options.D: Local university professors

explanation: Missionaries established the first Western medical facilities and basic training initiatives in various parts of Nigeria during the colonial era. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why was adapting nursing training to local Nigerian disease patterns necessary after independence?

options.A: To ensure nurses were prepared to manage prevalent local conditions like malaria
options.B: To stop nurses from working in international hospitals
options.C: To completely ban foreign textbooks from all universities
options.D: To reduce the number of required clinical hours

explanation: Training needed to directly address the specific public health realities and disease burdens facing the Nigerian population. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: Manufacturing essential pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Regulating standards of nursing education and practice
options.C: Providing housing loans for registered nurses
options.D: Funding private hospitals across the country

explanation: The NMCN is the legal regulatory body tasked with controlling nursing education, registering practitioners, and maintaining professional discipline. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why has basic nursing education progressively shifted toward universities and polytechnics?

options.A: To replace doctors with nurse administrators
options.B: To eliminate the need for clinical hospital postings
options.C: To make nursing training shorter and less demanding
options.D: To elevate the academic rigor and critical thinking skills of practitioners

explanation: Integrating nursing into higher education ensures graduates possess deeper scientific knowledge and advanced problem-solving abilities for modern healthcare. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h4)

question: What fields are combined in the concept of nursing informatics?

options.A: Nursing science and information technology
options.B: Health insurance and accounting
options.C: Pharmacology and medical laboratory science
options.D: Hospital administration and architecture

explanation: Nursing informatics merges clinical nursing expertise with computer systems to manage and communicate health data effectively. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h5)

question: How does the use of electronic health records primarily benefit daily nursing workflow?

options.A: By ending all hospital night shifts
options.B: By allowing nurses to prescribe surgery without a doctor
options.C: By quickening access to patient history and reducing documentation errors
options.D: By completely removing the need to talk to patients

explanation: Digital records make patient data easier to read, update, and share securely among the healthcare team, cutting down on paperwork mistakes. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is evidence-based practice in nursing primarily built upon?

options.A: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values
options.B: Government financial budgets and insurance policies
options.C: Personal opinions of senior medical consultants
options.D: Strict hospital traditions and ancient folklore

explanation: EBP combines rigorous research findings with the nurse's clinical judgment and the preferences of the patient. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core component of evidence-based nursing practice?

options.A: Applying the nurse's practical clinical experience
options.B: Considering the personal preferences of the patient
options.C: Reviewing current scientific research journals
options.D: Relying solely on unwritten hospital gossip and workplace rumors

explanation: Unwritten gossip has no scientific validity; true evidence-based practice relies on proven research, expert skill, and patient context. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h6)

question: What term describes the mass migration of skilled Nigerian nurses to other countries for better opportunities?

options.A: Rural deployment
options.B: Clinical rotation
options.C: Brain drain
options.D: Mandatory posting

explanation: Brain drain refers to the departure of educated and experienced professionals from their home country seeking greener pastures abroad. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is a direct consequence of severe nursing shortages in local healthcare facilities?

options.A: Higher patient satisfaction scores across all wards
options.B: Faster turnaround times for hospital discharges
options.C: Immediate elimination of all public health diseases
options.D: Increased workloads and burnout among remaining staff

explanation: When fewer nurses are available to handle heavy patient loads, the remaining staff experience extreme fatigue and stress. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h7)

question: What does a holistic view of human health primarily include beyond the physical body?

options.A: Financial status and job title
options.B: Geographical location and housing
options.C: Political affiliation and education
options.D: Mental, social, and cultural aspects

explanation: Health involves a combination of physical, mental, social, and cultural factors rather than just physical well-being. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why must midwives look beyond a single physical symptom when caring for a pregnant woman?

options.A: Physical symptoms are usually completely unrelated to pregnancy
options.B: Health is a unique and broad human experience affecting the whole person
options.C: Mental health has no impact on physical body functions
options.D: Hospital regulations require checking social status first

explanation: Because health encompasses many dimensions of a person's life, care must address more than just isolated physical signs. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does the World Health Organization broadly define health?

options.A: Having a normal body temperature and pulse
options.B: Just the physical absence of any body pain
options.C: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.D: The ability to work without taking a break

explanation: The WHO definition emphasizes overall well-being across physical, mental, and social domains rather than just being free of sickness. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h2)

question: What makes illness different from a diagnosed medical disease?

options.A: Illness only occurs when a laboratory test is positive
options.B: Disease can never be cured, while illness always disappears quickly
options.C: Illness is a subjective feeling of being unwell, even without a formal diagnosis
options.D: Disease affects the mind while illness affects only the skin

explanation: Illness describes the personal, subjective experience of discomfort and disrupted function that a person feels inside. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h2)

question: What does the health-illness continuum represent?

options.A: A sliding scale showing health as a constantly changing state
options.B: A strict set of rules for diagnosing malaria
options.C: A laboratory test measuring blood sugar levels
options.D: A fixed medical category that never changes over time

explanation: The continuum portrays health not as a fixed point, but as a dynamic range moving between wellness and illness. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h3)

question: A pregnant woman with severe morning sickness moves toward which end of the health-illness continuum temporarily?

options.A: The permanent immunity end
options.B: The illness and poor health end
options.C: The optimal wellness and peak fitness end
options.D: The complete absence of physical form

explanation: Experiencing debilitating symptoms shifts a person closer to the illness side of the continuum until relief and recovery occur. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which health model defines wellness strictly as the absence of physical signs of disease?

options.A: Eudaimonistic model
options.B: Clinical model
options.C: Role performance model
options.D: Adaptive model

explanation: The clinical model focuses narrowly on the medical signs of sickness and considers a person healthy if no disease is found. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the main focus of the role performance model of health?

options.A: How well a person adjusts to sudden climate changes
options.B: Having normal blood pressure and laboratory results
options.C: A person's ability to fulfill work and family duties
options.D: Achieving high spiritual and emotional happiness

explanation: This model evaluates health based on whether an individual can successfully carry out their expected daily roles in society. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an internal variable that influences health beliefs?

options.A: Genetic makeup and emotional state
options.B: Availability of local healthcare clinics
options.C: Cultural traditions of the community
options.D: Socioeconomic status and income

explanation: Internal variables arise from within the individual, such as genetics, age, and emotional maturity. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why should a midwife understand the cultural background and family practices of a pregnant woman?

options.A: Hospital policies require documenting family ancestry charts
options.B: Family practices replace the need for physical examinations
options.C: External variables strongly shape health beliefs and health-seeking behaviors
options.D: Cultural background determines blood type during delivery

explanation: Culture and family background are external factors that heavily influence how a patient views illness and makes health choices. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is a common impact of serious illness on a household?

options.A: Immediate increase in household income
options.B: Disruption of family roles and financial strain
options.C: Complete elimination of household stress
options.D: Permanent stabilization of family routines

explanation: Illness places emotional and financial pressure on a family while forcing others to take over the duties of the sick member. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important for midwives to consider the whole family when a mother is ill?

options.A: Family members are legally required to pay hospital bills
options.B: Household members always share the exact same physical disease
options.C: Illness in one member affects the daily functioning of the entire family
options.D: Midwives are trained to treat family legal issues

explanation: Because a household is interconnected, sickness in a mother changes roles and causes stress for everyone involved. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary focus when care is guided by basic human needs?

options.A: Reducing the cost of medications
options.B: Treating the whole person
options.C: Following strict facility routines
options.D: Speeding up hospital discharge

explanation: Looking at basic human needs ensures midwives care for the entire individual rather than focusing solely on a specific disease diagnosis. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why do hospitalized patients often struggle to meet their own basic needs?

options.A: Patients completely forget their daily habits during admission
options.B: Hospital regulations forbid patients from caring for themselves
options.C: Healthcare workers prefer to complete all tasks for the patient
options.D: Illness and unfamiliar hospital environments cause temporary loss of independence

explanation: Sickness and a strange environment strip away a person's usual ability to care for themselves, requiring nursing support. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which level sits at the absolute base of Maslow's human needs pyramid?

options.A: Love and belonging
options.B: Self-esteem needs
options.C: Safety and security
options.D: Physiological needs

explanation: Physiological requirements like oxygen and water form the foundational base of the pyramid because life cannot continue without them. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h2)

question: A woman is admitted with severe pre-eclampsia and intense anxiety about her unborn baby. According to need hierarchies, what should the midwife address first?

options.A: Ask her family to visit and comfort her
options.B: Help her feel confident about her room
options.C: Stabilize her dangerously high blood pressure
options.D: Counsel her on the fears of motherhood

explanation: Life-threatening physical instability must always be managed before addressing psychological concerns like anxiety. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is classified as a physiological need?

options.A: Personal growth
options.B: Oxygen
options.C: Friendship
options.D: Self-respect

explanation: Oxygen is a vital physical requirement needed directly by body tissues to sustain life. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why do midwives prioritize monitoring fluid balance in surgical or postpartum patients?

options.A: To ensure the patient finishes their hospital meals
options.B: To reduce the amount of paperwork at shift change
options.C: To prevent life-threatening shock and organ failure
options.D: To keep the patient awake during daytime hours

explanation: Fluids maintain blood volume and pressure, protecting vital organs from failing due to dehydration or hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which nursing action directly addresses a patient's physical safety need?

options.A: Raising bed rails and keeping the environment free of clutter
options.B: Allowing the patient to choose their afternoon meal
options.C: Praising the patient for following a low-salt diet
options.D: Encouraging visits from extended family members

explanation: Preventing accidental falls through environmental checks directly protects a patient's physical safety. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does explaining a clinical procedure beforehand help satisfy a patient's security needs?

options.A: It reduces fear of the unknown and builds trust in the provider
options.B: It speeds up the time it takes to complete the treatment
options.C: It guarantees that no complications will occur during care
options.D: It eliminates the need to obtain written consent

explanation: When patients understand what is about to happen, anxiety drops and their sense of psychological security increases. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which intervention best supports a hospitalized patient's need for love and belonging?

options.A: Providing a strict schedule for medication administration
options.B: Checking vital signs every four hours without interruption
options.C: Ensuring the patient's room is kept at a cool temperature
options.D: Welcoming family members to participate in visiting hours

explanation: Involving family members helps maintain vital emotional connections and reduces feelings of isolation during illness. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is a likely consequence if a patient's psychosocial need for belonging is completely ignored?

options.A: Rapid weight gain due to lack of physical movement
options.B: Feelings of depression and delayed emotional healing
options.C: Immediate physical infection at the surgical site
options.D: A sudden rise in blood pressure and body temperature

explanation: Isolation and lack of social support frequently contribute to low mood and can hinder overall recovery. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h5)

question: What does preserving patient dignity primarily help to protect?

options.A: Infection control
options.B: Self-esteem
options.C: Fluid balance
options.D: Physical survival

explanation: Treating a patient with respect and preserving their privacy directly supports their sense of self-worth and esteem. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h6)

question: A newly delivered mother feels useless because she needs help bathing and changing her baby. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Guide her gently through tasks at her own pace and praise her efforts
options.B: Ask a relative to take over baby care duties until she goes home
options.C: Tell her that every new mother feels this way and leave the room
options.D: Take over completely so she does not feel stressed by failure

explanation: Involving the mother in small steps builds her confidence and restores her sense of competence and self-esteem. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h6)

question: What describes the concept of self-actualization in patient care?

options.A: Maintaining stable blood pressure and normal body temperature
options.B: Complying strictly with a hospital medication timetable
options.C: Attaining financial security after paying hospital bills
options.D: Reaching one's full potential and finding personal meaning

explanation: Self-actualization represents the highest level of personal growth, fulfillment, and realization of one's capabilities. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is supporting higher-level needs like self-actualization important during rehabilitation?

options.A: It shortens the length of hospital stays during acute surgical recovery
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never be readmitted to the hospital
options.C: It replaces the need for standard medical diagnostics and lab tests
options.D: It empowers patients to take charge of their long-term health and lifestyle

explanation: Helping patients find purpose and personal goals motivates them to maintain healthy habits long after discharge. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h7)

question: When organizing a busy shift, which category of needs must a midwife manage first?

options.A: Belonging needs
options.B: Physiological needs
options.C: Self-esteem needs
options.D: Self-actualization

explanation: Physiological survival needs are the most urgent and must always take clinical priority over higher-level psychosocial needs. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h8)

question: A patient is crying in pain from a fresh surgical incision while asking for her husband. Which action demonstrates correct priority setting?

options.A: Ask the husband to administer the pain medication before entering
options.B: Bring the husband in immediately and ignore the pain medication request
options.C: Administer prescribed pain relief first, then invite the husband inside
options.D: Delay all interventions until both problems can be solved together

explanation: Managing physical pain and physiological comfort takes priority, followed swiftly by addressing the emotional need for family support. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of national professional nursing organizations?

options.A: To provide free medical treatment to rural communities
options.B: To unite practitioners, protect public health, and advance the profession
options.C: To manage hospital budgets and hire medical doctors
options.D: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local clinics

explanation: These organizations exist to bring nurses together, safeguard the health of the public through high standards, and push the profession forward. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h1)

question: How do national nursing bodies connect individual clinicians to government decisions?

options.A: By providing a collective voice for policy influence
options.B: By directly writing laws without legislative approval
options.C: By collecting taxes from every registered nurse
options.D: By appointing government ministers of health

explanation: Instead of individual nurses trying to reach lawmakers alone, these bodies pool numbers and authority to influence health policies. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main legal responsibility of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To regulate nursing education and protect the public
options.B: To provide financial loans for building private clinics
options.C: To negotiate better salaries and housing allowances for nurses
options.D: To supply medical equipment to public hospitals

explanation: The council is a regulatory body, meaning its main job is to set standards and protect the public, not to act as a salary-negotiating trade union. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following functions does the NMCN NOT perform?

options.A: Disciplining nurses who commit professional misconduct
options.B: Issuing practicing licenses to qualified practitioners
options.C: Accrediting nursing training institutions and programs
options.D: Negotiating annual salary increases with the government

explanation: Salary negotiations and welfare issues are handled by trade unions, whereas the NMCN focuses strictly on regulation, licensing, and discipline. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h2)

question: What primary function does NANNM perform for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: Registering student nurses at the start of training
options.B: Inspecting nursing schools for curriculum approval
options.C: Defending their socio-economic welfare and working conditions
options.D: Conducting professional board examinations and licensing

explanation: NANNM operates as a trade union, focusing on workers' rights, salaries, and workplace safety rather than board examinations. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is it important to distinguish NANNM from the NMCN?

options.A: One is a trade union for welfare, while the other is a regulatory body for standards
options.B: One handles only male nurses, while the other registers only midwives
options.C: One functions exclusively in hospitals, while the other works in communities
options.D: One operates under the Ministry of Education, while the other is private

explanation: Knowing the difference prevents confusion; NANNM fights for your welfare and pay, while the NMCN sets your rules and licenses you. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of specialty nursing associations in Nigeria?

options.A: To provide international scholarships for all nursing students
options.B: To promote excellence and best practices in specific clinical fields
options.C: To handle national strike actions for hospital workers
options.D: To replace the regulatory functions of the Nursing and Midwifery Council

explanation: Specialty groups bring together nurses with shared clinical interests, such as pediatrics or surgery, to advance knowledge and care standards in those specific areas. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h4)

question: A staff nurse working exclusively in the hospital operating theater would most likely join which specialty body?

options.A: Accident and Emergency Nurses Association of Nigeria
options.B: National Association of Paediatric Nurses of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses in Academia
options.D: Perioperative Nurses Association of Nigeria (PTONAN)

explanation: Perioperative nurses work in surgical suites and operating theaters, making PTONAN the appropriate specialty association for them. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h4)

question: How do professional nursing organizations directly impact public health outcomes?

options.A: By advising governments on health crises and maternal care strategies
options.B: By manufacturing vaccines for distribution to clinics
options.C: By paying the monthly salaries of all government nurses
options.D: By building private pharmacy shops in rural communities

explanation: National bodies use their collective expertise to guide government action on major health issues like maternal mortality and disease outbreaks. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is one way nursing organizations help standardize clinical procedures?

options.A: By purchasing uniform medical equipment for all teaching hospitals
options.B: By assigning patients to specific hospital beds daily
options.C: By publishing clinical practice guidelines for safe patient care
options.D: By grading student semester examinations in universities

explanation: Professional organizations formulate guidelines that tell clinicians the safest, most evidence-based ways to carry out procedures. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a major advantage for a student nurse who joins a professional nursing association early?

options.A: Receiving automatic exemption from final board licensing exams
options.B: Gaining early networking, mentorship, and leadership opportunities
options.C: Getting free accommodation in hospital staff quarters
options.D: Being appointed immediately as a senior nursing officer

explanation: Early membership introduces students to mentors, conferences, and leadership roles that build their professional confidence. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h6)

question: How does professional socialization during student years benefit a future midwife?

options.A: It helps them adopt the values, ethics, and identity of the profession
options.B: It eliminates the need for practical clinical hospital postings
options.C: It guarantees them a scholarship to study abroad after graduation
options.D: It teaches them how to bypass hospital management protocols

explanation: Professional socialization is the process of absorbing the core values, ethics, and culture expected of a practicing nurse or midwife. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of connecting nurses through international organizations?

options.A: To create a unified voice for the profession
options.B: To recruit nurses away from developing nations
options.C: To replace local nursing councils entirely

options.B: Laboratory scientists
options.C: Consultant surgeons
options.D: Hospital administrators

explanation: Nurses and midwives constitute the bulk of clinical staff, providing continuous 24-hour observation and patient care in wards and units. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is a multi-disciplinary health team approach necessary in secondary health facilities?

options.A: Hospital management boards require all staff to share administrative duties equally
options.B: Different specialists are needed to manage complex medical and surgical conditions effectively
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to write patient care reports
options.D: It ensures that doctors do not have to work night shifts in the wards

explanation: Complex health issues require combined expertise from doctors, midwives, pharmacists, and lab scientists to achieve the best patient outcome. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the term for sending a patient from a primary health clinic to a General Hospital due to a complication?

options.A: Upward referral
options.B: Community outreach
options.C: Downward discharge
options.D: Lateral transfer

explanation: Moving a patient from a lower level of care to a higher, more specialized facility is known as an upward referral. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h5)

question: How does a well-functioning referral system benefit tertiary teaching hospitals?

options.A: It allows them to focus exclusively on community health outreach programs
options.B: It ensures they only admit patients who cannot afford any medical bills
options.C: It removes the need for them to employ specialist doctors and nurses
options.D: It prevents them from becoming overcrowded with cases that secondary facilities can handle

explanation: By filtering cases through primary and secondary tiers, tertiary hospitals can concentrate on highly complex sub-specialty cases and advanced research. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which government body typically oversees the administration of public secondary health facilities in Nigerian states?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Education
options.B: Local Primary Health Care Authority
options.C: Hospital Management Board
options.D: National Universities Commission

explanation: State Hospital Management Boards or Ministries of Health hold the direct administrative responsibility for public General Hospitals. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary role of the Director of Nursing Services within a secondary health facility administration?

options.A: To represent the state government in legal disputes involving patients
options.B: To procure all surgical instruments and pharmaceutical drugs for the hospital
options.C: To manage the financial accounts and revenue collection of the entire hospital
options.D: To oversee nursing and midwifery personnel, standards of care, and nursing administration

explanation: The Director of Nursing Services coordinates the nursing workforce, ensures professional standards are maintained, and advises management on nursing matters. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h6)

question: What term describes the mass migration of skilled health workers like doctors and midwives from Nigeria to other countries?

options.A: Rural drift
options.B: Upward referral
options.C: Brain drain
options.D: Clinical rotation

explanation: Brain drain refers to the emigration of trained professionals seeking better working conditions abroad, leaving local facilities understaffed. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical operational challenge faced by many public secondary health facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: Frequent power outages requiring expensive generator fuel
options.B: Excessive surplus of modern medical equipment and staff housing
options.C: Inadequate funding and budgetary allocations from the government
options.D: Shortages of essential drugs and consumable supplies

explanation: Public secondary facilities struggle with shortages and lack of equipment, rather than experiencing an excessive surplus. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which level of Nigeria's health care system serves as the primary responsibility of local government councils?

options.A: Primary health care
options.B: Secondary health care
options.C: Tertiary health care
options.D: Quaternary health care

explanation: Primary health care is designed to be closest to the grassroots and is managed primarily at the local government level. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the main function of tertiary health facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: Providing highly specialized medical and surgical care
options.B: Providing temporary shelter for displaced community members
options.C: Handling routine immunizations and community health talks
options.D: Managing basic normal deliveries at the village level

explanation: Tertiary centers sit at the top of the referral chain to handle complex cases that lower levels cannot manage. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h1)

question: What are the three core mandates of tertiary health institutions in Nigeria?

options.A: Specialized clinical care, training, and research
options.B: General outpatient care, retail pharmacy, and optical services
options.C: Primary immunization, community mobilization, and sanitation
options.D: Traditional medicine integration, drug manufacturing, and taxation

explanation: Tertiary health institutions are uniquely mandated to provide advanced treatment, train healthcare students, and conduct medical research. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why are tertiary hospitals often called teaching hospitals in Nigeria?

options.A: They focus exclusively on teaching patients how to cook healthy meals
options.B: They only open their doors to student lectures and never treat sick patients
options.C: They are closely tied to universities for training medical and nursing students
options.D: They are schools where primary school teachers go for routine checkups

explanation: Teaching hospitals combine patient care with the academic training of doctors, midwives, nurses, and other health professionals. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which unit in a tertiary hospital is specifically equipped to care for critically ill newborn babies?

options.A: General Outpatient Department
options.B: Environmental Health Unit
options.C: Medical Records Department
options.D: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit

explanation: The Neonatal Intensive Care Unit houses incubators and specialized equipment to manage premature or critically ill newborns. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h3)

question: How do outpatient clinics in tertiary hospitals typically receive their patients?

options.A: Through mandatory door-to-door community screening exercises
options.B: By inviting only pregnant teenagers for mandatory registration
options.C: Mostly through referrals from lower-level health facilities
options.D: By selecting random individuals from local market squares

explanation: Tertiary outpatient clinics are designed to receive patients who have been referred upward from primary or secondary centers. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which professional group do midwives work most closely with in a tertiary maternity complex?

options.A: Agricultural extension officers
options.B: Financial accountants
options.C: Obstetrician-gynecologists
options.D: Civil engineers

explanation: Midwives in tertiary maternity complexes collaborate directly with obstetrician-gynecologists to manage complex childbirth cases. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h4)

question: A pregnant woman presents with severe high blood pressure and convulsions at a primary health centre. Where should she be sent?

options.A: Tertiary maternity complex with an intensive care unit
options.B: Traditional birth attendant for herbal steaming and massage
options.C: Primary health clinic antenatal registry for next month
options.D: Local chemist shop for immediate over-the-counter tablets

explanation: Eclampsia is a severe emergency requiring the advanced multispecialty care available in a tertiary maternity complex. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h4)

question: Who serves as the chief executive officer responsible for daily administration in a federal teaching hospital in Nigeria?

options.A: Chief Medical Director
options.B: Director of Public Works
options.C: Local Government Chairman
options.D: Honorable Minister of Education

explanation: The Chief Medical Director is the head of management tasked with overseeing the clinical and administrative operations of a federal teaching hospital. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the Board of Management in a tertiary health institution?

options.A: Setting broad policy guidelines and overseeing institutional governance
options.B: Personally performing emergency surgeries during night shifts
options.C: Dispensing drugs across hospital pharmacy counters to patients
options.D: Sweeping and cleaning the hospital premises every morning

explanation: Boards of management provide governance, policy direction, and oversight rather than direct clinical execution. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h5)

question: What term describes the process of sending a stabilized patient from a tertiary hospital back to a local primary health center for follow-up?

options.A: Upward escalation
options.B: Emergency discharge
options.C: Mandatory quarantine
options.D: Downward referral

explanation: Downward referral moves patients back to lower levels of care once specialized tertiary intervention is complete. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why does going directly to tertiary hospitals instead of primary and secondary facilities create problems in the health system?

options.A: It forces doctors at tertiary hospitals to stop performing major surgeries
options.B: It prevents patients from ever buying drugs from retail pharmacies
options.C: It makes the primary health centers completely empty of all health workers
options.D: It overburdens tertiary facilities with minor ailments meant for lower levels

explanation: When patients bypass primary centers for simple issues, tertiary specialists spend time on routine cases instead of complex emergencies. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which activity is a core duty of tertiary health institutions alongside patient care?

options.A: Collecting local government tenement rates and taxes
options.B: Building trunk roads and maintaining public electricity grids
options.C: Issuing international passports and national identity cards
options.D: Conducting health research and training students

explanation: Teaching hospitals and tertiary centers are legally mandated to train healthcare professionals and conduct medical research. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h7)

question: How do clinical postings in tertiary hospitals benefit student midwives?

options.A: They provide direct exposure to high-risk obstetric cases and advanced care
options.B: They teach students how to construct hospital buildings
options.C: They allow students to manage hospital finances and budgets
options.D: They exempt students from taking classroom examinations

explanation: Exposure in tertiary settings allows midwifery students to handle complex clinical scenarios they may not see at primary clinics. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h7)

question: What does the term "brain drain" refer to in the context of Nigerian tertiary health care?

options.A: The closure of university medical schools due to protests
options.B: The mass emigration of skilled healthcare professionals abroad
options.C: The removal of outdated books from hospital libraries
options.D: A medical condition caused by severe mental exhaustion

explanation: Brain drain describes the loss of trained doctors, nurses, and midwives who leave the country for better opportunities overseas. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge in Nigerian tertiary health facilities?

options.A: Frequent electricity grid failures and heavy reliance on generators
options.B: Breakdown of advanced diagnostic machines with delayed repairs
options.C: High reliance on out-of-pocket payments by struggling patients
options.D: Excessive availability of surplus specialist staff in all departments

explanation: Tertiary facilities face severe staff shortages rather than a surplus of specialist personnel. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h8)

question: What term is commonly used for someone receiving preventive care in the community?

options.A: Casualty
options.B: Patient
options.C: Client
options.D: Inmate

explanation: The term client is used for active participants in community-based and preventive health services. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why does a person usually change from being a client to a patient when entering a hospital?

options.A: They shift from seeking wellness to requiring acute medical treatment
options.B: They become completely immune to community health education
options.C: They lose all legal rights to make decisions about their own body
options.D: They stop paying for health services out of pocket

explanation: Entering a hospital usually means the individual is seeking treatment for a specific illness, making them a patient. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main focus of healthcare interactions with a community client?

options.A: Intensive care unit monitoring
options.B: Surgical management of acute trauma
options.C: Palliative end-of-life sedation
options.D: Primary prevention and health promotion

explanation: Community healthcare focuses on keeping people well through health promotion, immunization, and disease prevention. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h2)

question: A pregnant woman attending a village health post for routine antenatal talks is best described as:

options.A: An acute care patient
options.B: A community client
options.C: A surgical casualty
options.D: A critical care resident

explanation: Attending a local post for routine health promotion while remaining independent makes her a community client. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h2)

question: What main factor often increases a person's vulnerability upon admission to a health institution?

options.A: Immediate appointment to a leadership board
options.B: Complete freedom to direct hospital schedules
options.C: Excessive availability of home-cooked meals
options.D: Loss of personal control and unfamiliar routines

explanation: Hospital admission places individuals into strict institutional routines, reducing their autonomy and increasing vulnerability. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h3)

question: How should midwives balance institutional rules in a maternity ward?

options.A: Ignoring hospital protocols in favor of total patient freedom
options.B: Allowing patients to manage their own complex surgical procedures
options.C: Protecting the patient's dignity while maintaining clinical safety
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital rules without listening to complaints

explanation: Midwives must respect personal dignity and agency while following necessary safety guidelines. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which environment places the healthcare provider on unfamiliar ground within the care recipient's personal space?

options.A: Private clinic office
options.B: Institutional theatre
options.C: Tertiary hospital ward
options.D: Community setting

explanation: In community care, the midwife visits the client's home or local territory, which changes the dynamic of control. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why can a rigid hospital environment negatively impact some patients?

options.A: It forces them to adapt to strange routines and unfamiliar clinical settings
options.B: It forces healthcare workers to abandon all safety protocols
options.C: It grants them too much authority over hospital administrative staff
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never want to return home

explanation: Strange noises, shared spaces, and rigid hospital rules can cause anxiety and reduce patient comfort. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h4)

question: What action helps reduce risks when transferring a client from a primary clinic to a general hospital?

options.A: Providing clear referral notes and effective handover communication
options.B: Allowing the client to travel without any documentation
options.C: Encouraging the family to bypass hospital registration
options.D: Withholding clinical history until the patient recovers fully

explanation: Clear notes and handovers ensure the receiving facility understands the clinical history and urgency of the case. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is a major danger of poor transitions between community care and institutional care?

options.A: Delays in receiving life-saving treatment for sudden complications
options.B: Immediate discharge of all hospitalized patients back home
options.C: Unwanted promotion of the client to a healthcare provider role
options.D: Excessive reduction in the cost of hospital medications

explanation: Poor communication and transport delays during transitions can lead to severe health consequences. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h5)

question: What does patient advocacy primarily involve in clinical midwifery practice?

options.A: Protecting patient rights and ensuring informed consent
options.B: Making all medical decisions on behalf of the family
options.C: Enforcing hospital financial policies over patient welfare
options.D: Preventing clients from asking questions about treatment

explanation: Advocacy means standing up for the patient's rights, choices, and right to be fully informed about their care. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h6)

question: A midwife notices a doctor using complex medical terms that a frightened patient does not understand. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Advise the patient to discharge themselves immediately without treatment
options.B: Break down the explanation into simple terms and ensure the patient understands
options.C: Tell the patient to stop asking questions and obey the medical team
options.D: Ignore the situation because doctors are solely responsible for communication

explanation: The midwife acts as an advocate by ensuring true informed consent through simple, clear explanations. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h6)

question: What primary group surrounds a patient in a Nigerian community alongside the nuclear family?

options.A: Extended family
options.B: Government regulators
options.C: International agencies
options.D: Hospital board members

explanation: Extended family networks form a core part of the immediate social structure influencing healthcare choices in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why do midwives look beyond the individual patient during health assessments?

options.A: Patients rarely remember their own medical history accurately.
options.B: Hospital policies mandate interviewing at least three relatives.
options.C: Family and community relationships shape health decisions and recovery.
options.D: Midwives lack the time to assess single patients on their own.

explanation: Patients are influenced by their surrounding social structures, which affect how they perceive illness and follow treatment plans. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h1)

question: Who often holds the main authority for approving medical care in many traditional family settings?

options.A: Elected local government chairmen
options.B: Household heads and family elders
options.C: External religious leaders only
options.D: The youngest child in the home

explanation: Family elders and household heads traditionally guide major financial and health-related decisions within the home. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the best action when a patient wants treatment but says her husband must approve it first?

options.A: Refuse care until the patient changes her cultural beliefs.
options.B: Invite the spouse to take part in the health counseling session.
options.C: Ignore the husband and start treatment immediately.
options.D: Tell the patient she is legally independent and needs no one else.

explanation: Involving key decision-makers respects family dynamics and improves compliance by securing collective agreement. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h2)

question: What common duty do family members often take on during a patient's hospital stay in Nigeria?

options.A: Providing bedside care, cooking, and supporting daily needs
options.B: Auditing the hospital financial accounts daily
options.C: Prescribing medications to the patient
options.D: Performing major surgical procedures in the ward

explanation: Family members in many Nigerian hospitals actively assist with physical care, feeding, and supplying daily necessities. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h3)

question: How does a mother's prolonged illness directly affect the broader household?

options.A: Government grants immediately replace any lost daily earnings.
options.B: Income drops and resources stretch as family members spend time caregiving.
options.C: Household expenses automatically decrease due to lower food consumption.
options.D: Community members take over all financial responsibilities permanently.

explanation: A mother's illness disrupts household productivity and diverts funds toward medical costs and caregiving logistics. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which local group in Nigeria helps mobilize resources and maintain primary health facility infrastructure?

options.A: Ward Development Committees
options.B: International trade unions
options.C: Foreign diplomatic missions
options.D: Private banking syndicates

explanation: Ward Development Committees work closely with health facilities to support community health initiatives and infrastructure. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why is building a working relationship with Traditional Birth Attendants important for midwives?

options.A: It allows TBAs to perform major surgeries inside the hospital.
options.B: It prevents pregnant women from visiting community markets.
options.C: It helps ensure timely referral of high-risk pregnant women to formal facilities.
options.D: It replaces the need for professional midwives in rural health posts.

explanation: Since many women visit TBAs first, cooperating with them builds a bridge for safe referrals during obstetric emergencies. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the appropriate response when a patient mentions a traditional health belief that is harmless?

options.A: Refuse to treat her until she abandons her cultural heritage.
options.B: Report her to local law enforcement authorities immediately.
options.C: Scold the patient publicly to stop her from talking about it.
options.D: Respect the harmless belief while providing safe care.

explanation: Midwives practice cultural competence by respecting harmless traditions while addressing only those practices that threaten health. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way to handle harmful cultural health practices?

options.A: Provide patient education explaining the health risks.
options.B: Listen patiently to understand the root cause of the practice.
options.C: Involve respected community elders to advocate for safer alternatives.
options.D: Ridicule the patient's family for being backward.

explanation: Ridicule damages trust and drives patients away from formal health facilities, whereas respectful education encourages change. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of inviting partners to attend antenatal education sessions?

options.A: They pay for all hospital staff salaries directly.
options.B: They replace the need for laboratory investigations.
options.C: They take over midwifery clinical duties in the labor ward.
options.D: They learn about danger signs and support birth preparedness.

explanation: Involving partners ensures they recognize pregnancy complications early and actively assist with birth plans. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h6)

question: How can a midwife best approach a mother-in-law who insists on giving a newborn water alongside breast milk?

options.A: Allow her to feed the baby whatever she wants without speaking up.
options.B: Educate her respectfully on the benefits of exclusive breastfeeding for six months.
options.C: Threaten to discharge the mother and baby from the clinic instantly.
options.D: Ignore her and tell the new mother to disobey her in secret.

explanation: Respectful dialogue that enlists the older relative as an ally works much better than threats or outright dismissal. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the main role of the midwife when a patient first arrives at the health facility?

options.A: Serving as the primary face and guide of the institution
options.B: Ordering all medical supplies from central storage
options.C: Handling hospital financial accounting and billing audits
options.D: Managing structural facility maintenance and repairs

explanation: Nurses and midwives are usually the first health professionals patients meet, which makes them key in helping clients navigate the facility. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is a smooth transition between hospital departments important for a client?

options.A: It removes the responsibility of care from the primary midwife
options.B: It ensures the patient leaves the facility within one hour
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any clinical documentation
options.D: It reduces client anxiety and builds trust in the health system

explanation: Clear and organized movements help ease the emotional and physical stress patients feel when navigating a new care environment. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a quick triage assessment when a patient arrives?

options.A: Completing the entire hospital billing and payment process
options.B: Assigning a permanent room number for inpatient admission
options.C: Gathering detailed family medical history for research
options.D: Quickly identifying emergency conditions requiring immediate care

explanation: Triage allows staff to spot life-threatening issues right away so urgent treatment can begin without delay. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h2)

question: A pregnant woman arrives at the clinic showing signs of severe pre-eclampsia. What should be the immediate priority?

options.A: Request full payment of hospital fees before any evaluation
options.B: Ask her to return home with a relative for paperwork
options.C: Direct her to join the regular queue and wait her turn
options.D: Initiate prompt clinical assessment and medical attention

explanation: Emergency conditions require immediate clinical action rather than routine administrative delays. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard step during formal inpatient admission?

options.A: Confirming the patient's identity using an identification band
options.B: Securing informed consent for planned treatments
options.C: Performing major surgical operations immediately on arrival
options.D: Recording baseline vital signs and obstetric history

explanation: Surgery is not a routine part of admission for every patient entering the ward. Admission focuses on assessment, documentation, and orientation. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why is recording baseline vital signs upon admission crucial for midwives?

options.A: It replaces the need for continuous monitoring during labor
options.B: It fulfills a legal requirement to discharge the patient early
options.C: It provides a reference point to detect future clinical changes
options.D: It determines the exact financial cost of the hospital stay

explanation: Baseline measurements let health providers spot sudden changes by comparing current status to the values recorded at admission. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a midwife before transferring a patient to a higher-level facility?

options.A: Discharging the patient completely from all medical follow-up
options.B: Collecting full cash payment for the upcoming hospital stay
options.C: Booking commercial transport without notifying the receiving hospital
options.D: Stabilizing the client's condition as much as possible

explanation: A patient must be stabilized before transfer to handle the journey and reduce the risk of their condition worsening on the way. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is direct communication with the receiving facility essential during a patient referral?

options.A: To cancel all previous diagnostic lab test results
options.B: To allow the transferring midwife to negotiate treatment costs
options.C: To transfer legal ownership of the patient's personal property
options.D: To ensure the receiving team expects the patient and prepares necessary resources

explanation: Calling ahead alerts the destination team so they can ready the labor room, blood bank, or specialists before the patient arrives. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h4)

question: At what point in the hospital stay should discharge planning ideally begin?

options.A: During the final financial billing process
options.B: On the exact morning of departure
options.C: At the point of admission
options.D: One week after the patient returns home

explanation: Starting discharge planning early ensures that health education and home care preparations happen gradually without rushing the patient. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h5)

question: A nursing mother is ready to leave the maternity ward. What combination of tools best ensures she understands her home care instructions?

options.A: Handing over her medication bottles without any explanation
options.B: Strictly waiting for family members to guess her care needs
options.C: Verbal counseling combined with a written discharge summary
options.D: Directing her to read a medical textbook independently

explanation: Using both verbal and written communication reinforces learning and gives the patient a reliable guide to check at home. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which regulatory body oversees professional nursing and midwifery practice in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Economics Association
options.B: National Union of Road Transport Workers
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Internal Affairs

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria sets the standards for training, practice, and professional conduct across the country. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is a major legal risk of failing to document clinical care during admission or discharge?

options.A: It can lead to professional negligence claims and disciplinary action
options.B: It automatically increases the hospital's financial revenue
options.C: It ensures faster processing of patient health insurance claims
options.D: It prevents any future communication with the patient

explanation: Accurate records serve as legal proof of care given. Missing documentation leaves the nurse unprotected during legal disputes. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the main goal of health education in nursing and midwifery practice?

options.A: To replace formal medical diagnosis in rural clinics
options.B: To fulfill mandatory administrative documentation tasks
options.C: To change behavior and promote healthy lifestyles
options.D: To reduce the total number of hospital admission days

explanation: Health education is designed to guide individuals toward adopting healthy habits and preventing illness before it occurs. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h1)

question: A midwife explains exclusive breastfeeding to a new mother at a primary health care center. What kind of activity is this?

options.A: A diagnostic laboratory investigation step
options.B: An emergency pharmacological treatment protocol
options.C: A routine administrative admission procedure
options.D: A core clinical health education intervention

explanation: Teaching a mother about breastfeeding is a direct educational activity aimed at improving maternal and child health outcomes. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is active participation important when teaching adult patients?

options.A: It legally protects the hospital from future malpractice claims
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any follow-up visits
options.C: Adults learn and retain information better when they are involved
options.D: Patients prefer doing all the talking during consultation sessions

explanation: Active participation engages the learner's critical thinking and practical skills, leading to better retention than passive listening. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h2)

question: What does the term 'readiness to learn' mean in patient education?

options.A: The learner must be physically and emotionally prepared to receive information
options.B: The government must fund the community outreach program fully
options.C: The clinic must have printed pamphlets available in local languages
options.D: The nurse must have completed all required university teaching modules

explanation: Readiness to learn means the patient's current state allows them to focus on and process educational content effectively. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why should a midwife assess a patient's learning needs before starting health education?

options.A: To determine the exact financial income of the patient
options.B: To select which doctor will perform the surgery
options.C: To avoid teaching things the patient already knows
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital accreditation paperwork

explanation: Assessment ensures that teaching is targeted, efficient, and directly relevant to the specific gaps in the patient's knowledge. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to patient learning in a clinic?

options.A: Physical pain and overwhelming fatigue
options.B: High levels of anxiety and emotional distress
options.C: Language differences and low literacy levels
options.D: Possession of a valid health insurance card

explanation: Insurance status affects healthcare access and payment, but it does not directly obstruct learning in the way pain, language gaps, or anxiety do. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why is the demonstration and return demonstration method so effective for teaching practical skills?

options.A: It allows the nurse to verify that the patient can perform the skill correctly
options.B: It takes less time than explaining the procedure with a textbook
options.C: It completely replaces the need for verbal instructions or warnings
options.D: It requires no special equipment or training materials from the clinic

explanation: Having the patient perform the return demonstration proves they have understood and mastered the physical steps required. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which teaching method works best for discussing sensitive personal health matters with a patient?

options.A: Large group lectures
options.B: Printed wall posters
options.C: One-on-one discussion
options.D: Community radio broadcast

explanation: Private one-on-one conversations create a safe, confidential space for patients to share personal concerns and ask sensitive questions. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why are nurses and midwives uniquely positioned to provide continuous health education?

options.A: They are the only healthcare workers trained in basic human anatomy
options.B: They control the hospital budget for educational materials
options.C: They possess legal authority to write prescriptions independently
options.D: They spend more direct time with patients than other health professionals

explanation: Continuous bedside and clinic contact gives nurses and midwives frequent, natural opportunities to teach and reinforce healthy behaviors. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h5)

question: What does it mean when a midwife acts as a 'role model' in health education?

options.A: The midwife acts in instructional videos produced by the ministry of health
options.B: The midwife dresses up in cultural attire for community drama events
options.C: Patients observe and are influenced by the midwife's personal and professional habits
options.D: The midwife models plaster of Paris for orthopedic teaching sessions

explanation: Actions speak loudly in healthcare; patients frequently emulate the attitudes and health practices they observe in their nurses and midwives. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h5)

question: A midwife finishes teaching a pregnant woman about danger signs. How can the midwife best check if learning occurred?

options.A: Give the patient a lengthy written essay test on obstetric complications
options.B: Document in the register that health education was successfully completed
options.C: Assume the patient understands because she nodded during the talk
options.D: Ask the patient to explain the danger signs back in her own words

explanation: The teach-back method is a practical way to check comprehension and ensure the patient grasped the key educational points. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the main difference between immediate evaluation and long-term evaluation of health education?

options.A: Immediate is done by doctors, while long-term is handled strictly by hospital administrators
options.B: Immediate costs money, whereas long-term evaluation is completely free of charge
options.C: Immediate checks understanding right away, while long-term looks at lasting health outcome changes
options.D: Immediate relies on written tests, while long-term relies entirely on guessing patient compliance

explanation: Immediate evaluation assesses short-term comprehension, whereas long-term evaluation measures sustained behavioral change and health status improvements. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of a professional interpersonal relationship in nursing?

options.A: Building a long-lasting personal friendship
options.B: The health and recovery of the client
options.C: Sharing personal life stories with patients
options.D: Completing administrative paperwork quickly

explanation: Unlike social friendships, the professional relationship is strictly centered on meeting the health needs of the patient. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why are professional relationships in healthcare different from everyday social friendships?

options.A: They require no emotional investment from the nurse
options.B: They are built on mutual sharing of personal problems
options.C: They last forever regardless of clinical discharge
options.D: They are completely one-sided and serve the client's needs

explanation: Professional relationships focus entirely on the patient's well-being rather than mutual social exchange. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h1)

question: During which phase of the therapeutic relationship do the nurse and client first meet and set initial trust?

options.A: Orientation phase
options.B: Working phase
options.C: Termination phase
options.D: Evaluation phase

explanation: The orientation phase is the initial meeting where introductions happen and the foundation of trust is laid. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h2)

question: A woman is being discharged from the postnatal ward after a successful delivery. What phase of the nurse-client relationship is taking place?

options.A: Working phase
options.B: Orientation phase
options.C: Pre-interaction phase
options.D: Termination phase

explanation: Discharge marks the end of the professional bond, which is the termination phase. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of asking open-ended questions during a client assessment?

options.A: It prevents the client from asking questions back
options.B: It shortens the time needed for documentation
options.C: It encourages the client to share detailed feelings
options.D: It forces the client to give a quick yes or no

explanation: Open-ended questions allow patients to express their thoughts and concerns fully in their own words. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?

options.A: Explaining how to breastfeed the baby
options.B: Asking the patient where she feels pain
options.C: Maintaining an open posture and nodding
options.D: Reading hospital admission guidelines aloud

explanation: Body language, posture, and facial expressions are forms of non-verbal communication. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h3)

question: What does a professional boundary in nursing primarily do?

options.A: Prevents doctors from speaking with midwives
options.B: Ensures patients pay their hospital bills on time
options.C: Keeps the relationship focused strictly on client care
options.D: Stops the nurse from ever talking to patients

explanation: Boundaries ensure that the interaction remains safe, therapeutic, and centered on the patient's healthcare needs. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which action by a nurse represents a clear violation of professional boundaries?

options.A: Referring a pregnant woman to a social worker
options.B: Explaining the hospital visiting hours clearly
options.C: Sitting quietly while a mother expresses grief
options.D: Borrowing money from a patient on the ward

explanation: Borrowing money or entering financial dealings with a patient crosses the line into exploitation and violates professional boundaries. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the best approach when caring for a client who speaks a language you do not understand?

options.A: Skip the health education session entirely
options.B: Use a qualified professional interpreter
options.C: Speak very loudly in your native language
options.D: Ask the patient's young child to translate

explanation: Using a trained interpreter ensures accuracy and protects patient confidentiality, unlike using family members or children. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective clinical communication?

options.A: Clear and simple spoken language
options.B: Loud noise in the hospital ward
options.C: Severe pain and physical discomfort
options.D: Cultural differences in health beliefs

explanation: Clear and simple language actually helps communication rather than acting as a barrier. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is teamwork and good communication among different healthcare workers important?

options.A: It ensures that staff members never disagree on duty
options.B: It stops nurses from having to document patient care
options.C: It allows doctors to avoid speaking with pregnant women
options.D: It prevents medical errors and keeps patients safe

explanation: Clear communication among all members of the healthcare team ensures coordinated care and prevents dangerous mistakes. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h6)

question: What role does a midwife often play within the broader interprofessional healthcare team?

options.A: Prescribing complex specialist drugs independently
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of the hospital
options.C: Making final decisions on major surgical operations
options.D: Advocating for the mother and bridging communication gaps

explanation: Midwives spend the most time with childbearing women and act as a voice for them when coordinating with doctors and specialists. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of communication in nursing practice?

options.A: Completing hospital paperwork quickly
options.B: Preventing patients from asking questions
options.C: Building trust and assessing patient needs
options.D: Directing staff members during emergencies

explanation: Communication forms the foundation of the nurse-patient relationship, allowing midwives to build trust and properly understand clinical needs. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why does effective communication matter during antenatal care visits?

options.A: It replaces the need for physical clinical examinations
options.B: It guarantees that the baby will be born without complications
options.C: It stops patients from changing their clinic days
options.D: It helps reduce patient anxiety and improves compliance

explanation: When patients feel heard and understood, they are less anxious and more likely to follow medical advice and return for follow-up visits. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?

options.A: Facial expressions and body posture
options.B: Explaining the stage of labor out loud
options.C: Reading a health education pamphlet
options.D: Writing in the patient case notes

explanation: Non-verbal communication involves physical cues like body posture, eye contact, and facial expressions rather than spoken words. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h2)

question: A midwife tells a worried mother that everything is fine while frowning and crossing her arms tightly. What problem does this create?

options.A: The mother will fail to understand the spoken words
options.B: Physical examination results will become inaccurate
options.C: Hospital management will penalize the midwife
options.D: Mixed messages create patient distrust
